## Design the experience before the screen

Name the audience, their goal and the shortest useful path through the page. **UI** is the visible controls and presentation; **UX** is the larger experience of understanding, acting, receiving feedback and recovering from mistakes.

Plan:

- hierarchy: what should be noticed first, second and third;
- layout: related items group together with usable spacing;
- navigation: links are labelled clearly and the current location is understandable;
- states and feedback: selected, loading, success, empty and error where relevant;
- responsive thinking: content reflows and remains readable on a phone;
- files and paths: image filenames, folders and links remain valid after publishing;
- accessibility: semantic headings, meaningful alternative text, keyboard access, contrast and readable motion.

## Small TAS task

Create one simple page or portfolio that reuses the student's original identity, graphics and optional 2–4 second animation. Include a short project explanation, process evidence and one reflection. Test it on a narrow and wide screen, then publish using the teacher-approved location.

This is a communication task, not a full programming curriculum. A polished template is not successful if the audience cannot understand the work or the student cannot explain the file structure and decisions.

## Usability evidence

Ask one person to find a specific project and explain its purpose without coaching. Record task completion, wrong turns, unclear labels and comments. Revise the structure before adding decoration.

## Free web and UI/UX resources

Use [MDN Learn Web Development](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development) for structured HTML, CSS, and JavaScript learning; [web.dev Learn](https://web.dev/learn/) for modern browser practices; [W3C WAI](https://www.w3.org/WAI/fundamentals/) for accessibility; [WebAIM's Contrast Checker](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/) for a quick colour test; and [GitHub Pages documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pages) for static-site publishing. The [full free-resource directory](../resources/index.qmd) includes additional coding, icon, font, colour, and validation tools.
